Smurfs.API: Hosts JWT accounts and authenticated Smurf list, detail, create, edit, and delete endpoints, serves the React client, and exposes Swagger.
Smurfs.Application: Defines the MediatR create, list, details, edit, and delete handlers. It owns request/results and the filtered, sorted read contract and coordinates domain validation and persistence.
Smurfs.Domain: Defines Smurf, Pet, and Village and the domain rules that apply to them. It owns the name validation rule and registers it in the Smurfs business-rule catalog.
Smurfs.Infrastructure: Implements the application's Smurf read service against the app-data EF Core context. It orders, pages, and projects results for the list use case. It also provides the shared Serilog rolling file setup used by the console and WPF.
Smurfs.Persistence: Defines the Smurfs persistence contracts for the Smurf repository, app-data initialization, and unit-of-work creation and lifetime.
Smurfs.Persistence.EFCore.AppData: Stores the shared Smurf model with selectable PostgreSQL or SQLite providers, independent migrations and snapshots, repositories, unit of work, initialization, and seed data.
Smurfs.Persistence.EFCore.Identity: Owns the separate ASP.NET Core Identity store, including the user model, shared EF Core context, provider contexts with independent PostgreSQL and SQLite migrations, and sample-account seeding.
Smurfs.UI.Avalonia: Hosts the Avalonia desktop interface for loading and paging through Smurfs using the shared view model.
Smurfs.UI.Console: Hosts initialization, creation, and paged listing commands with selectable SQLite, PostgreSQL, or JSON file persistence and shared application handlers.
Smurfs.UI.WinForms: Hosts the Windows Forms catalog browser and adapts the shared paging commands and state to WinForms controls.
Smurfs.UI.WPF: Hosts the Windows desktop interface. It composes services at startup and supplies the windows and dialogs for browsing the catalog and creating a Smurf.
Smurfs.ViewModel: Provides the presentation state and commands for the WPF catalog and create dialog. It dispatches application requests through MediatR and exposes results and validation feedback to the views.
Smurf.Persistence.EFCore.AppData.UnitTes: Exercises SQLite persistence, application handlers, filtered and sorted reads, provider migration discovery and snapshots, and Identity integration. React component/store tests live in Smurfs.WebClient. File integration tests exercise real temporary catalogs, application handlers, conflicts, invalid files, and initialization.
Smurfs.Persistence.File: Stores the catalog in a versioned JSON file. Implements tracked unit-of-work snapshots, repository queries, initialization, shared sample data, filtered/paged reads, atomic replacement, and revision conflict detection.
Smurfs.Persistence.API: Implements authenticated HTTP sign-in and the application Smurf read contract against Smurfs.API. Tokens stay in memory. The repository/unit-of-work classes remain unregistered write skeletons for a later milestone.
Smurfs.UI.Console.API: Signs in to a running Smurfs.API and browses adjacent pages through the HTTP read adapter. No EF Core, Identity store, local catalog initialization, or write commands are registered.
